title: Retries preserve order (fictional example)
summary: Persistence must succeed before cursor advancement. Source references in this example are fictional.

background.text: A worker processes job-42. Its cursor identifies the current job, while the store holds completed results.

intuition.text: On failure the cursor stays at job-42. On success, storing its result permits advancement to job-43. The flow shows dependencies; the sequence shows interaction order.

code.text: In fictional src/worker.py lines 40–41, persistence returns before cursor assignment. An exception exits before advancement. A crash between these operations can still cause repeated processing.

code.title: Invariant
code.text: The current result becomes durable before the cursor advances.

quiz.question: What closes the job-skipping failure window?

options.text: The cursor advances after persistence confirms durable storage.
options.feedback: Failed persistence exits before the assignment.

options.text: The worker sorts jobs before attempting durable storage.
options.feedback: Sorting does not govern advancement.

options.text: The client retries requests before checking worker status.
options.feedback: Client retries do not govern the cursor.

options.text: The scheduler duplicates jobs before assigning available workers.
options.feedback: Duplication does not close the failure window.

quiz.question: Where does the cursor point after persistence raises?

options.text: It identifies the current job for another attempt.
options.feedback: The assignment was never reached.

options.text: It identifies the next job for immediate processing.
options.feedback: Advancing would recreate the skip.

options.text: It identifies the first job in every batch.
options.feedback: There is no batch rewind.

options.text: It identifies no job until all workers stop.
options.feedback: Worker availability is unrelated.

quiz.question: What does a successful persistence response establish?

options.text: The current result is durable before advancement begins.
options.feedback: The store has confirmed the write.

options.text: Every active worker has finished its assigned batch.
options.feedback: There is no worker barrier.

options.text: The requesting client has stopped sending retry attempts.
options.feedback: The response says nothing about clients.

options.text: All pending jobs are sorted by submission time.
options.feedback: Persistence does not sort jobs.

quiz.question: Which path avoids the cursor assignment?

options.text: Persistence raises while storing the current job result.
options.feedback: The exception prevents reaching the assignment.

options.text: Persistence returns after storing the current job result.
options.feedback: The assignment follows the return.

options.text: The worker starts with the current job selected.
options.feedback: That is normal initial state.

options.text: The queue receives a new job during processing.
options.feedback: Receiving work does not cause this exit.

quiz.question: What risk remains if the worker crashes after persistence?

options.text: The current job may run again before advancement.
options.feedback: A crash before assignment leaves the old cursor, permitting repeated work.

options.text: The next job must disappear from durable storage.
options.feedback: No operation removes the next job.

options.text: Every queued job must lose its stored result.
options.feedback: The change does not erase results.

options.text: The client must receive a successful retry response.
options.feedback: A crash guarantees no such response.
